text.tspan: Buildings and streets form a city neighborhood.
When we explore a neighbourhood, a little care can make the experience better. Planning and thinking
First, walking slowly helps us notice details we usually miss. For example, we stop to look at a doorway
instead of hurrying to the next landmark. This is a small thing that makes the day easier.
Second, respecting local routines makes a visit more considerate. For example, we keep an entrance
clear while taking a photograph of the street. We do not need a perfect day to do this well.
We can explore a neighbourhood more easily when we prepare and notice other people. These simple
steps give us a useful place to start.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the
conclusion. Each body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the
argument rather than introduce a new proposal.
You want to explore a neighbourhood, but one thing is difficult. Say what it is and give two ways to help. Use four short
paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: say what you want to do;
explain the first step; explain a different second step; say why the two steps help.)
